relevance_note: The cohort includes three probands (P6, P7, P8) with TNFAIP3 variants: 'haploinsufficiency of A20 (HA20; three cases)'.
method_note: Read the full Markdown. A Python script (scratch only) transcribed Tables 1 and 2 by splitting each row into cells and built spans as contiguous row prefixes from the patient label through the cited cell; I checked its output against both tables, and every value comes from my reading. Rows: the 10 SAID+ probands P1-P10 of Tables 1-2 (TNFAIP3: P6, P7, P8; RELA: P1-P5; GATA2: P9; trisomy 8: P10). The 24 ped-BD patients are reported only in aggregate, so they have no rows. The fathers of P6 and P8 (source of the TNFAIP3 variant per Table 1) get no rows: they have no label or clinical data in the text, and the pedigrees are in Figure 1, which is not in the text. P3 is labelled 'P3 (P2’s daughter)'; the paper calls both P2 and P3 probands. Variant descriptions (cDNA/protein) are not in the text (Figure 1 only), so variant_original_string is 'not reported' for the nine gene variants. P10's trisomy 8 is recorded as a variant row without a gene symbol. 'de novo' (P1, P7, P9, P10) is recorded as inheritance 'not reported' under rule 8, because the paper does not state that parental testing showed the variant absent in both parents; the label is kept in parental_testing_statement. Zygosity is 'not reported': only a cohort-level remark ('loss-of-function variant in one allele is compatible with the described dominant mode of inheritance'). Variant type is 'not reported': the paper says only 'All of the variants (except for trisomy 8) are predicted to result in frameshift or truncation' without saying which. Age columns are in years (headers 'Age at onset (years)' and 'Age at diagnosis (years)'); ISO durations keep the decimal year as printed (e.g. P0.08Y, P0.75Y, P2.5Y). Age at last evaluation is not given; follow-up months are given, but no age. Group exclusions: Table 3 gives 0 in the 'SAID+ (n = 10)' column for 'Neurological manifestations' and 'Vascular signs'. The SAID+ group is enumerated in Table 1, so both are recorded as excluded for all 10 ('inferred from group statement'), and 'central nervous system involvement' is excluded. 'Positive pathergy test' (0) was not used, because untested patients may be counted as negative. Patient eligibility exclusions (positive anti-ENA, RF, anti-CCP; confirmed infection) were not turned into phenotype rows. Checklist mapping choices: Table 1 'fever' was mapped to 'recurrent fever' as observed. The text reports 'recurrent fever episodes (7/10...' and Table 1 lists fever for exactly seven. 'cutaneous signs' was mapped to skin lesions. P4 'ocular signs' was NOT mapped to uveitis/ocular inflammation, because inflammation is not stated. Neutropenia and thrombocytopenia were NOT mapped to 'cytopenia (autoimmune)', because no autoimmune basis is stated. P9's acute lymphoblastic leukemia was NOT mapped to lymphoproliferation. ANA positivity (7/10), CRP and ESR are group-level only, so not reported. Contradictions or inconsistencies: (1) P6: Figure 3 oral-ulcer pathology 'consistent with vasculitis' vs Table 3 'Vascular signs' = 0 for SAID+. Both rows are emitted and the vasculitis checklist item is 'not reported' for P6. For the other nine, vasculitis is also left 'not reported', because 'vascular signs' is not clearly the same as vasculitis. (2) Table 3 'Cutaneous manifestations' SAID+ = 4, but Table 1 lists 'cutaneous signs' for 3 (P3, P4, P10). (3) The text says tocilizumab was given in 'two cases', but Table 2 shows it for 1 (P3). Table 3 treatment counts (steroids 8, colchicine 4, thalidomide 7, csDMARDs 4) differ from Table 2, where the script counts steroids 9, colchicine 5, thalidomide 8 and MTX/HCQ/SMZ/AZA 6. (4) Table 3 mean age of diagnosis 12.75 vs a mean of 12.85 computed from Table 1 (mean onset 4.383 matches 4.38). (5) P3: text 'recurrent oral ulcers since birth' vs Table 1 onset 0.08 years. (6) Pediatric cohort, but Table 1 ages at diagnosis include 28 (P2, the mother of P3), 23, 21 and 18. Note: Figure 4 uses 'P1', 'P2' and 'P3' for flow-cytometry cell populations, not patients; these were not used as patient labels.
